result:
Compiled successfully on the first try.

I wrote `tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 4 test class (JUnit 4.12 is present in `lib/` alongside 3.8.2) covering:

- Structural tokens (`beginArray`/`endArray`/`beginObject`/`endObject`, empty and non-empty, including `peek()` typing via `JsonToken`)
- Number/string interchangeability documented at the class level (numbers read as strings and vice versa)
- Boundary values (`Long.MAX_VALUE`, negative ints) and documented `NumberFormatException` cases (int/long overflow, non-finite/malformed doubles)
- Documented `IllegalStateException` cases (wrong token type for `nextString`/`nextBoolean`/`nextNull`/`nextDouble`/`nextLong`, and reads after `close()`)
- `nextName()`'s documented `IOException` when the token isn't a property name
- Structural mismatches (`beginObject` on an array, `endArray`/`endObject` called too early) asserted generically since the javadoc doesn't pin an exception type there
- `setLenient`/`isLenient`, the documented lenient behaviors (top-level non-object/array values, non-execute prefix)
- `skipValue()` over nested arrays/objects
- `END_DOCUMENT` token at stream end, `close()` closing the underlying `Reader` (verified with a custom `Reader` fixture), and non-null `getPath()`/`toString()`

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
